**Annexure – II**

**Terms, Conditions and General Applicability of the Tariff Order 2023-24**

*(This Annexure forms an integral part of the Tariff Order No. JESL/TO/2023-24 dated 31 March 2023, issued by the Rajasthan Electricity Regulatory Commission to Jaipur Electrical Supply Ltd. All provisions herein are effective from 1 April 2023.)*

---

**7. APPLICABILITY OF TARIFF**

7.1 The tariffs specified in Table 1 of the main order shall apply to all consumers receiving supply of electricity from Jaipur Electrical Supply Ltd (JESL) within its licensed area of supply, unless specifically exempted under the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003, or by a separate order of the Commission.

7.2 The tariff is applicable on a monthly billing cycle basis. For consumers billed on a bimonthly or quarterly cycle, the applicable charges shall be computed on the basis of the actual consumption recorded during the billing period, and the demand charges shall be levied on the maximum demand recorded in any month within that billing period.

7.3 Consumers falling under more than one category shall be billed under the category corresponding to the predominant use of supply, as determined by the connected load and the actual usage pattern. In case of dispute, the matter shall be referred to the designated officer of JESL whose decision, subject to appeal to the Commission, shall be final.

7.4 Mixed-use premises (residential-cum-commercial) shall be billed under the commercial category unless the residential portion is separately metered and the connected load of the residential portion does not exceed 3 kW, in which case separate billing may be allowed at the discretion of JESL.

---

**8. METERING ARRANGEMENTS**

8.1 All new connections and all existing connections with a sanctioned load of 10 kW and above shall be provided with smart prepayment meters, wherever technically feasible. The cost of the meter shall be borne by JESL, and the meter shall remain the property of JESL. In case of damage to the meter due to negligence or tampering by the consumer, the cost of replacement shall be recovered from the consumer at the actual procurement cost.

8.2 Meter readings shall be taken at intervals not exceeding one month for all categories except agricultural consumers, for whom the interval may be extended up to two months, subject to mutual agreement between JESL and the consumer.

8.3 If a meter is found defective, burnt, or stopped, the consumption for the period during which the meter remained defective shall be assessed on the basis of the average consumption of the preceding three months, or the corresponding period of the previous year, whichever is higher. In cases where no such data is available, the assessment shall be made based on the connected load and the hours of use as determined by JESL.

8.4 Consumers are required to provide safe and accessible premises for meter installation and reading. If a consumer prevents access to the meter on three consecutive occasions, JESL may issue a notice and, after giving 15 days' time, may estimate the consumption on the basis of the sanctioned load and the average usage pattern of the preceding billing period.

8.5 Check metering: JESL may install check meters at its own cost on the premises of any consumer for the purpose of verifying the accuracy of the consumer's meter. The consumer shall provide all reasonable facilities for the installation and reading of such check meters.

---

**9. BILLING AND PAYMENT**

9.1 Bills shall be issued by JESL on or before the due date specified in the billing cycle. The due date for payment of the bill shall be a minimum of 15 days from the date of issue of the bill.

9.2 Payment of the electricity bill shall be made by the consumer by the due date through any of the following modes: online payment portal, authorised payment gateway, designated bank branches, or any other mode as may be notified by JESL from time to time. A payment receipt shall be issued for all payments received.
